# Retry function attributes not working correctly

I found an issue with the retry function attributes in tenacity. When trying to modify the retry behavior of a wrapped function, it doesn't work as expected.

## Description

When using a function decorated with `@retry`, the `retry` attribute of the wrapped function is incorrectly set to the function itself instead of the retry object. This makes it impossible to modify the retry behavior after the function has been decorated.

## Steps to reproduce

```python
from tenacity import retry, stop_after_attempt, RetryError

@retry(stop=stop_after_attempt(3))
def my_function():
    # Some code that might fail
    return None

# Try to modify the retry behavior
my_function.retry.stop = stop_after_attempt(1)  # This doesn't work!

# Call the function
my_function()  # Still retries 3 times instead of 1
```

The issue is that `my_function.retry` is pointing to `my_function` itself instead of the retry object, creating a circular reference. This makes it impossible to modify the retry behavior after the function has been decorated.

This affects both synchronous and asynchronous retry functions.

## Expected behavior

The `retry` attribute of the wrapped function should point to the retry object, not to the function itself. This would allow modifying the retry behavior after the function has been decorated.

actions.old_string:
# Preserve attributes
        wrapped_f.retry = wrapped_f  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
        wrapped_f.retry_with = retry_with  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
        wrapped_f.statistics = {}  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
actions.new_string:
# Preserve attributes
        wrapped_f.retry = self  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
        wrapped_f.retry_with = retry_with  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
        wrapped_f.statistics = {}  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
